original.description: Objective: To develop a low SwaP breadboard of a full laser system that will manipulate Rydberg atom in vapour cell, and be able tobe configured for sensing applications for RF receivers.Description: Highly-excited atoms, often known as Rydberg atoms, display extreme sensitivity to external electromagnetic (EM) fields, including the electric fields associated with black-body radiation (BBR).In addition to their use in quantum computing, Rydberg atoms can be configured for sensing applications. Such sensors make use of non-destructive read-out of Rydberg states, which is implemented optically, including fluorescence detection of low-lying Rydberg states. A range of different Rydberg sensing modalities have been developed; these include those developed for microwave standards andimaging in the Terahertz regime to sensitive digital communications techniques in radio and microwave bands. This activity developsa complete laser system needed to perform an RF instrument based on Alkali Rydberg Atomic Sensors. To do so the selection of the relevant parameters to address the sensor is aimed to be done by consolidating the first set of requirements. A dedicated focus is to be addressed towards a low SWaP (Size, Weight and Power) for CubeSAT platform. This shall ensure a proper design and manufacturing of the Laser system. This breadboard is then tested on an adequate Rydberg sensor for RF measurement. The activity encompasses the following tasks: - Requirement review for laser system to manipulate Rydberg atom - Design of a compact laser system - Manufacturing of the laser system - Test on Rydberg Atom and validation of the RF instrument.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activities in open competition limited to the-non-Large-System Integrators. original.description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to design a satellite system for FRMCS which is operating in the same frequency bands as the terrestrial counterpart (i.e., 900 MHz and 1.9 GHz), with the purpose to exclusively service the coverage gaps of the terrestrial network while avoiding interference. The performance of such system will be evaluated with the development of a system simulator.Targeted Improvements: - Reduce by 80% the cost of the satellite system for FRMCS.- Reduce by 50% the cost of on-board railway terminals, by allowing a single terminal solution for terrestrial and satellite FRMCS connectivity.Description: The Future RailwayMobile Communication System (FRMCS), being a successor of the GSM-R system, is planned to be operational before GSM-R's predicted saturation in 2030. Through standardisation work, satcom is established as a component of the future system, while it is found that the satellite integration into FRMCS is simplified when satcom is employing the 5G NR, which is the selected air interface for the terrestrial FRMCS access. However, the frequency bands for such a service via satellite and the design of the satellite system are yetto be concluded. The advantages of an innovative approach, where the satellite offers connectivity exclusively to the coverage gapsofsuch terrestrial network, have been recently reported. In fact, such a satellite system targeting only the terrestrial coverage gaps while ignoring the areas serviced by theterrestrial network, will have a lower complexity and overall cost, as fewer satellites of less capacity will be required. In addition, such a satellite system will be able to operate in the same frequency bands as theterrestrial network (i.e., 900 MHz and 1.9 GHz), as each network (terrestrial or satellite) will not be available in the same area where the other network operates and therefore they will not interfere with each other. This usage of the same frequency from the satellite and the terrestrial network not only facilitates the integration of the two networks into FRMCS, but also potentially allow the usage of the same terminal for both networks, a solution that is very favourable for railway operators. This activity will thereforeinvestigate the design of a 5G NR based satellite system for FRMCS which exclusively targets the terrestrial network gaps of communication and operates in the same frequency bands as the terrestrial FRMCS network. The activity will include a traffic characterisation and capacity analysis for the terrestrial network gaps which will then feed the system design and the element sizing of the ground and space components. The impact of the railway-satellite channel for the 900 MHz and the 1900 GHz will also be thoroughly investigated. The best numerologies and 5G NR configurations will also be identified for such a satellite system. The work will be supported by the development of a system simulator which will investigate the FRMCS 5G NR satellite link performance and achieved C/I ratios under a variety of different orbits, system architectures, frequency bands, channel conditions and air interface configurations. The activity will also investigate and conclude on the feasibility of having a single modem and a single antenna equipped on board the trains, which offer connectivity both to the satellite and the terrestrial network at different time instances.

original.description: Objective: To develop a comprehensive set of rigorously tested tools that ensures monitoring, risk assessment, and collision avoidance for close proximity operations.Description: Past activities related to Close Proximity Operations (CPO) highlighted the need ofdeveloping low impact velocity tools that can verify and validate that the servicer spacecraft (SC) maintains a collision risk probability of less than given threshold (e.g 10^-4) with the client SC during CPO. For missions involving multiple SC in close formation, the design of manoeuvres to avoid collisions with catalogue objects not belonging to the formation requires to take into account all SC of the formation, e.g. an avoidance manoeuvre performed by one SC of the formation shall not trigger an inner-formation collision risk but rather minimise disturbance to the formation while ensuring the required risk reduction. This activity aims at developing a comprehensive set of tools (e.g. DRAMA like tool, prototype software for formation flying) that ensure monitoring, risk assessment, and collision avoidance during close proximity operations (including formation flying). This activity encompasses the followingtasks: - Develop and refine software tools that model the trajectory of both the target and servicer. - Develop algorithms that identify safe trajectories for close approaches and include collision avoidance features. - Develop tools that perform uncertainty propagation to estimate the likelihood of a collision between the servicer and client. - Identify sensor systems capable of providing design and operational level data about the relative positions, velocities, and orientations of both the servicer and the target. - Conduct virtual testing within the developed tools to simulate close approach and rendezvous operations in various scenarios. - Develop mathematical models of constraints and requirements and prototype a software solution suitable for realistic scenarios.

original.description: As part of the Greek National Satellite Space Project - Phase 2, the objective of this activity is the procurement of Phase A/B1 for an In-Orbit Demonstration (IOD) mission aimed at the development and in-space demonstration of a flexible small-satellite platformenabling future In-Space Servicing, Assembly and Manufacturing (ISAM) missions.The mission shall demonstrate autonomous rendezvous,inspection and close-proximity operations (CPO) capabilities in orbit, while supporting the development of European industrial andcommercial capabilities and fostering future operational services.The mission shall address identified user needs and market opportunities with the objective of contributing to the development of future European in-space infrastructure and services. Tenderers shall therefore propose a mission concept that combines technology demonstration objectives with a credible path towards future operational applications.The mission and system development approach shall be based on a modular and scalable architecture, supported byanincremental demonstration strategy with clearly defined primary and extended objectives. The proposed implementation shall prioritise mission success, schedule robustness and affordability, while enabling future capability growth. Primary objectives will focus on demonstrating autonomous rendezvous, inspection and close-proximity operations capabilities, including relative navigation, guidance and control, onboard autonomy, mission operations and payload-carrying capability. Secondary objectives may include extended CPO manoeuvres (V-bar and R-bar approaches), synchronised relative motion demonstrations, technology maturation activities for futureISAM missions, and payload accommodation demonstrations such as advanced sensors or robotics. The implementation of secondary objectives will be subject to available resources and mission opportunities, without compromising the achievement of the primary objectives.
